artifacts.notes: The press route https://press.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19641121_unitatis-redintegratio_en.html and content-delivery route https://www.vatican.va/content/dam/wss/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19641121_unitatis-redintegratio_en.html returned byte-identical 50959-byte responses with this SHA-256 on 2026-07-24; the aliases are not duplicated. The response contains the complete numbered body, translated promulgation formula and date, and consolidated notes. Delivered defects include article 2's «thou has», article 3's «embraces upon them», note 2's «Jn. 11, S2», note 11's Matthew 16:18 where the Latin and Acta witnesses give 16:19, note 15's «1 Petr. 2, 2S», «VATICANUM 1», and «Collac», note 22's «Enarr. 11», note 27's «LATERANSE», note 28's Ephesians 4:24 where the Latin gives 4:23, and note 36's «loannem». This list records known source-local defects without claiming an exhaustive diplomatic collation. Exact bytes are identified but not retained.

passages.context: The complete English article and its source notes were inspected for non-imputation of the original separation's sin to those now born into separated communities, imperfect communion through faith and valid Baptism, elements of sanctification and truth beyond visible Catholic boundaries, and the relation of separated Churches and communities to the Catholic fullness of the means of salvation.
passages.notes: Article 3's notes cite Scripture, the Councils of Florence, Lateran IV, and Lyon II, and Augustine's second enarration on Psalm 32. Those source-of-source citations do not make a publication using this article a direct consumer of the cited predecessors.

passages.context: The complete English range was inspected for the status of Christians and ecclesial realities outside full Catholic communion and for ecumenical practice: truthful and fair representation, competent dialogue, cooperation, common prayer where allowed, Catholic renewal, and the distinction between ecumenical action and individual reconciliation.
passages.notes: The range preserves both recognition of real Christian goods and the Decree's claims about incomplete communion and Catholic fullness. Its central verification does not authorize a consumer to suppress either side or to treat source-of-source notes as independently checked.

passages.context: The complete English article and its source note were inspected for integral and clear presentation of Catholic doctrine without false irenicism, precise explanation intelligible to separated Christians, dialogue in truth, charity, and humility, and the hierarchy of truths according to their relation to the foundation of Christian faith.
passages.notes: The hierarchy of truths orders doctrines by their relation to the Christian foundation; the article does not authorize omission, denial, or dilution of doctrine.

passages.context: The complete English article and its source note were inspected for Baptism duly administered according to Christ's institution, incorporation and rebirth in Christ, the sacramental bond among the baptized, Baptism's orientation toward full profession, incorporation, and Eucharistic communion, and the Decree's account of separated Western communities' Lord's Supper.
passages.notes: Article 22 joins recognition of Baptism's real sacramental bond to its stated incompleteness as only a beginning ordered toward full Christian life and Eucharistic communion. Its scriptural note is a source-of-source citation, not an automatic direct binding to Colossians or Romans.

work.author: Second Vatican Council
work.description: The Second Vatican Council's Decree on Ecumenism, solemnly promulgated by Pope Paul VI on 21 November 1964. Its numbered articles 1-24 state Catholic principles and practices for the restoration of Christian unity and address separated Eastern Churches and Western ecclesial communities.
work.title: Unitatis Redintegratio
